findings.statement: The institution with controlling authority also has interests in scientific continuity and reputation, creating a material conflict of interest.
Participants have no meaningful voice while the institution can determine access to treatment within the study design.
A1, A2 and A3 are less coercive feasible routes to preserve legitimate research or review objectives.

principle_assessments.reason: Continuation uses more power and imposes more harm than necessary because known feasible alternatives exist.
The decision structure lacks demonstrated independent scrutiny despite a strong institutional conflict and serious effects on life and health.
Internal objections have been raised; continuation without independent review risks insulating the programme from challenge.

information_requests: Who has authority to halt the programme independently of the institution running it?
alternatives_or_safeguards: Suspend under A3; transfer review to an independent ethics body; offer treatment immediately.
evidence_that_could_change_view: Evidence of truly independent oversight with authority to protect participants would reduce MC-11 concerns, but not justify untreated continuation on the present facts.
